name: a_index_closes
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Index closes & futures.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, Dow, Russell 2000, PHLX SOX closes (level, % change); S&P sector leaders/laggards; biggest index point contributors; index futures pre-market on the brief date (% change, time quoted).

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

- **S&P 500** closed at **7,746.41**, up **0.35%** on Thursday, October 15, 2026. (24/7 Wall St., Oct 15; publish time not shown)[8]
- **Dow Jones Industrial Average** closed at **52,231.50**, up **1.16%**. (24/7 Wall St., Oct 15; publish time not shown)[8]
- **Nasdaq Composite** gained **0.19%** on October 15. The available result does not provide a verified closing level. (24/7 Wall St., Oct 15; publish time not shown)[8]
- **Russell 2000** closed at **2,769.89**, up **1.42%**. (24/7 Wall St., Oct 15; publish time not shown)[8]
- The available results do not provide a verified **PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX)** closing level or percentage change for October 15. (Search results available through Oct 16 02:03 ET)[1][8]

## S&P sectors `[Macro]`
- **Health care** led the S&P 500 sector groups, gaining approximately **2.5%** during Thursday’s session; **Moderna (MRNA)**, **Veeva Systems (VEEV)**, and **Eli Lilly (LLY)** gained approximately **5.5%**, **5%**, and **5%**, respectively. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]
- **Technology and communications-related shares** lagged as AI-linked stocks declined; **Nvidia (NVDA)** fell nearly **2%**, while **Apple (AAPL)** fell **0.3%**. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]
- **Dell Technologies (DELL)** and **Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE)** were among the weakest S&P 500 performers, while **Seagate Technology (STX)** and **Western Digital (WDC)** pressured the memory-stock segment. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]

## Dow contributors `[Macro]`
- **Nike (NKE)** rose **6%**, while **Sherwin-Williams (SHW)**, **Home Depot (HD)**, **Walmart (WMT)**, and **McDonald’s (MCD)** also gained and supported the Dow’s advance. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]
- **Nvidia (NVDA)** and **Amazon (AMZN)** declined during the session and weighed on the Dow. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]

## Semiconductors `[Semiconductors]`
- The **iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX)** was approximately **1% lower** during Thursday’s session after falling **4.5%** on Wednesday; the available results do not provide a verified SOX index close. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]
- **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM)** fell **2%** on October 15 despite reporting record profit and exceeding estimates, according to the available market coverage. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[6]

## Index futures `[Macro]`
- The latest pre-market futures readings available in the results were **Dow futures up 0.3%**, **S&P 500 futures down 0.3%**, and **Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.1%**; the quoted time was not provided in the result. (Investopedia, Oct 15; publish time not shown)[1]
- At **4:04 a.m. ET on October 15**, Nasdaq 100 futures were down **1.26%**, S&P 500 futures were down **0.35%**, and Dow futures were up **0.39%**; this reading predates the requested October 16 pre-market window. (Beinsure, Oct 15, 04:04 ET)[4]
